set.per_unit_cap: Statutory: lower income units under Rev. and Tax. Code 214(g); units stay exempt if an existing tenant's income rises to 140% AMI in tax credit units or to 100% AMI in other agreement-restricted units (the 100% rule runs FY 2024-25 through 2028-29). Revenue and Taxation Code 214(g)(1)(C) caps the exemption at $20,000,000 of assessed value per taxpayer per fiscal year (single or multiple properties), and only where the exemption rests solely on the 90 percent lower income occupancy test for a property not owned by a limited partnership. Projects with tax-exempt bonds, government loans or grants (214(g)(1)(A)) or low-income housing tax credits (214(g)(1)(B)) are outside the cap; LP-owned projects with a nonprofit managing general partner must have tax credits or government financing to qualify (BOE Publication 149). Not a statewide cap.
set.prevailing_wage_basis: Property tax exemption; no construction funds are provided, so the exemption itself does not make a project public works.
set.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check Nov 9, 2026: the cited BOE county contacts page is only an assessor directory. Checked BOE Publication 149 and Rev. and Tax. Code 214 and 255. Eligibility covers any qualifying lower income rental project, not only supportive housing; the $20 million cap is per taxpayer and does not apply to LP projects or to projects with tax credits or government financing; the AB 84 language was about over-income tenants, not new 100% AMI units. Claims are due Feb 15 each year (filed annually, not a NOFA).

reason: Material: eligible_project_types limited the exemption to supportive housing and per_unit_cap misdescribed the $20 million cap as a statewide cap on non-tax-credit LP projects, both contradicted by Rev. and Tax. Code 214(g) and BOE Publication 149.
